clues: This city sits where the River Liffey meets a wide bay in the west of Europe. Mountains rise to the south of its streets.
Rain falls far less here than on the wet west coast. The city's sheltered east coast spot makes it the driest place in the whole land.
When the land won its freedom in 1922, this city became its capital. It took the top job for the free state that year.
The Book of Kells, a hand painted Gospel book from about the year 800, is on show here. Its pages burst with bright beasts, knots, and swirls.
Ireland is ruled from this city. It is the land's capital, and its largest city too.
